researchRun.stop_reason: One detailed Ultra Maritime organization bundle was evidence-complete, duplicate-clear, and ready for human review; the uncorroborated PA-4 label was recorded as a follow-up rather than proposed for publication.

proposed_record.reviewerRationale: Ultra Maritime is a high-value addition because authoritative public evidence connects its Dartmouth operation to Canadian design and production of towed arrays, sonobuoys and hull-mounted sonar; Royal Canadian Navy Halifax-class and River-class work; and a newly delivered containerized Sea Tracker system for DRDC experimentation. The profile gives BD users a clear view of the company's Canadian industrial role, the technologies it can bring to undersea missions, and the public organizations around current work. The candidate is rated high confidence because Canadian identity and programs are corroborated by ACOA, COVE, Royal Canadian Navy material and multiple first-party product or contract pages. The supplied Sea Tracker link is strong evidence for a 20-foot ISO containerized submarine-detection capability, but it does not name PA-4 or the Protecteur class. Publish the documented Sea Tracker relationship only; keep the operator-provided PA-4 context out of the public dossier until a durable public source explicitly supports it.

fieldEvidence.excerpt: ACOA identifies Ultra Maritime's Dartmouth base as a Canadian undersea-warfare operation that manufactures or integrates sonobuoys, hull-mounted sonar and towed acoustic arrays and supports Royal Canadian Navy and allied naval programs.

The government profile calls Dartmouth a towed-array centre of excellence, states that the arrays are developed and built in Canada, and identifies sonobuoy, hull-sonar and towed-array work at the site.
The official contact page lists Ultra Maritime's Canadian site at 40 Atlantic Street, Dartmouth, Nova Scotia B2Y 4N2, with the public telephone number +1 902 466 7491.
The supplied official announcement names Sea Tracker, its 20-foot ISO container format, DRDC experimentation, COVE and ACOA support; it does not identify PA-4 or the Protecteur class.

Ultra describes Sea Tracker as a modular submarine-detection capability in a standard 20-foot ISO container for uncrewed and non-traditionally crewed platforms that can integrate active, passive, surveillance and torpedo-defence towed technologies.

Because COVE describes a containerized system for at-sea evaluation of active and passive towed arrays and DRDC experimentation on future ASW concepts, the capability is a direct fit for the public Underwater ISR mission area.
The official description says Sea Tracker is designed for uncrewed and non-traditionally crewed platforms, supporting a moderate derived alignment to autonomous patrol and monitoring workflows.

Ultra's product page describes Sea Lancer as an open and modular family of towed sonar systems for detection, localization and classification across surface, subsurface, crewed and uncrewed platforms.
The documented detection, localization, classification and multi-platform acoustic functions map directly to the public Underwater ISR mission area.
Ultra documents the Sea Searcher family as fully digital hull-mounted sonar and acoustic transducer technology for navigation, early threat detection, target identification and tracking.
The Royal Canadian Navy lists Ultra hull-mounted and towed sonar within the ship's integrated underwater-warfare system, supporting direct relevance to Underwater ISR.
Ultra lists Sea Revealer sonobuoys for submarine detection and tracking, identifies Canadian-specification variants, and describes integration work for uncrewed aerial vehicles.
ACOA states that sonobuoys handled in Dartmouth are deployed from aircraft or ships to detect and localize submarines, mapping directly to Underwater ISR.
Ultra reports River-class contracts covering engineering support, spares, readiness activities, shore installation, sea trials and final acceptance for the new surface-combatant fleet.
The lifecycle scope supports readiness of the River-class hull-mounted sonar and torpedo-defence elements that underpin the fleet's Underwater ISR mission.
Ultra states that it is providing Sea Tracker to Defence Research and Development Canada for experimentation and development of next-generation anti-submarine-warfare concepts.
COVE identifies Ultra Maritime Canada as an industry partner in the containerized at-sea towed-array testing initiative and says Ultra will deliver Sea Tracker.
ACOA describes prior project funding, advocacy and current support for Ultra Maritime's Canadian defence and marine work, including its Mission Pod development.
Ultra reports a Canadian Surface Combatant hull-mounted-sonar production order from Lockheed Martin Canada and identifies itself as the program's anti-submarine-warfare lead.

organization.name: Ultra Maritime
organization.description: See the Canadian systems behind submarine detection at sea. From its Dartmouth operation, Ultra Maritime develops and builds towed arrays in Canada and manufactures or integrates sonobuoys, hull-mounted sonar, containerized Sea Tracker systems, and lifecycle support for Royal Canadian Navy and allied undersea-warfare programs.

profileData.canadianOperations: Dartmouth is Ultra Maritime Canada's primary public location and a towed-array centre of excellence. Public Canadian evidence ties the site to in-country towed-array development and production plus sonobuoy, hull-mounted-sonar and naval integration work.
profileData.evidencePosture: Public sources support the Sea Tracker name, its 20-foot ISO container format, and collaboration with DRDC, COVE and ACOA. They do not use the PA-4 or Protecteur-class identifiers, so those labels are not proposed for publication.

capabilities.name: Sea Tracker Containerized ASW System
capabilities.summary: Put frigate-grade submarine detection onto a wider range of ships and uncrewed platforms. Sea Tracker packages a scalable towed-sonar architecture in a standard 20-foot ISO container, giving operators a rapidly deployable way to integrate active, passive, surveillance and torpedo-defence arrays for experimentation or operational concepts.

applications: At-sea evaluation of next-generation towed arrays
Rapid deployment of submarine detection onto available vessels
DRDC experimentation and development of future anti-submarine-warfare concepts

missionMatches.alignmentSummary: Sea Tracker combines rapidly deployable submarine detection with active and passive towed-array integration, making it a direct fit for underwater detection, classification, tracking and experimentation.
The system is designed for uncrewed and non-traditionally crewed platforms, creating a credible path to add persistent undersea sensing to autonomous maritime patrol concepts.

capabilities.name: Sea Lancer Towed Sonar Arrays
capabilities.summary: Extend detection beyond a ship's hull and build a clearer picture of the undersea environment. The Sea Lancer family combines active and passive towed-sonar options with an open modular architecture for detection, localization and classification across crewed and uncrewed surface or subsurface platforms.

Open modular architecture with interoperable and interchangeable subsystems

Crewed, optionally crewed and uncrewed anti-submarine-warfare missions

missionMatches.alignmentSummary: Sea Lancer's detection, localization and classification functions give operators the acoustic coverage needed to find and understand submarine and torpedo activity across wider areas.

capabilities.name: Sea Searcher Hull-Mounted Sonar & Transducers
capabilities.summary: Give a ship a continuous inner layer of underwater awareness. Sea Searcher combines digital hull-mounted sonar with acoustic-transducer engineering to support navigation, early threat detection, target identification and tracking for surface-combatant and submarine missions.

missionMatches.alignmentSummary: Hull-mounted sonar provides persistent shipboard detection, classification and tracking at the centre of an integrated underwater-warfare picture.

capabilities.summary: Move submarine detection beyond the ship and across a larger search area. Sea Revealer includes active, passive and environmental sonobuoy variants for deployment from aircraft or ships, with Canadian-specification products and emerging integration paths for uncrewed aircraft.
